S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: A persistent perception that one is useless or inferior to others.
subtypes.Self-Criticism: Excessively and repeatedly blaming oneself for past minor failures or flaws.
subtypes.Reduced Self-Efficacy: Distrust in one's own ability to perform tasks or solve problems.
subtypes.Chronic Sense of Inferiority: Persistently evaluating oneself lower in comparison to others.
subtypes.Lack of Self-Assurance: Continually feeling anxious and unsure about decisions or actions.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a depressed mood lasting for at least two years in adults, accompanied by additional depressive features that cause clinically significant distress or functional impairment. It typically presents with a long-standing pattern of low mood, low energy, poor self-esteem, and cognitive or sleep changes that are less severe than major depressive episodes but more enduring. The course is often insidious, beginning in response to psychosocial stressors or temperament vulnerabilities and then becoming a persistent baseline state, sometimes punctuated by superimposed major depressive episodes (“double depression”). It is distinguished from Major Depressive Disorder primarily by its chronicity and often earlier, more gradual onset, and from normal sadness by its persistence, pervasiveness, and impact on functioning and quality of life.

patient.personality: She is driven, analytical, and socially engaged, channeling a competitive perfectionism into both her biomedical work and her artistic, community-oriented hobbies.
patient.stressor: About four years ago, Mattie took on a major grant-funded initiative to develop low-cost implantable devices for use in under-resourced hospitals, accepting responsibility for aggressive timelines, regulatory navigation, and cross-disciplinary coordination. As the project progressed, budget cuts, shifting regulatory requirements, and interpersonal conflicts with a new, metrics-obsessed department head led to repeated delays and public criticism of her leadership during meetings and review boards. Over the next three years she increasingly extended her work hours, sacrificed time for painting, jazz nights, and gardening, and began to doubt her professional judgment as younger colleagues advanced more visibly and a key pilot trial failed, which she internally interpreted as a personal failure rather than a systemic setback. The gradual erosion of her confidence and constant pressure to make high-stakes technical decisions despite feeling mentally "slower" eventually interfered with her ability to manage projects and mentor effectively, prompting her to seek psychiatric help when she found herself unable to organize complex tasks at work the way she used to.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like my mind just doesn’t work the way it used to and I can’t think things through or make decisions at work anymore.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest, like someone turned the dimmer switch down on my life, and even when something objectively good happens at work or with my kids I just feel flat and vaguely hopeless instead of excited.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I fall asleep exhausted around midnight, but I’m awake again at three or four in the morning with my mind quietly chewing on work problems and old mistakes, and then I just lie there, restless and unrefreshed, until the alarm goes off.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: Where I used to juggle complex design specs and regulatory documents in my head, now I find myself rereading the same paragraph three times, losing my train of thought in meetings, and agonizing over decisions that used to be almost automatic.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.
S042.manifestation: Over these last few years I’ve started to see myself as the weak link in the lab, telling myself that I’m a fraud who held everyone back on the grant and that my younger colleagues are advancing because they’re simply better than I ever was.
